issues.issue: Can the refusal rest on the late restoration filing, with the officer's other comments treated as obiter?
issues.applicant_position: Officer did not separate reasons from ancillary comments; all comments were part of the refusal.
issues.respondent_position: Refusal rested on the late restoration filing; other comments were observations only, akin to obiter.
issues.result_quote: The Respondent’s submission is not persuasive for two reasons.

issues.issue: Were the officer's factual findings (three prior restorations; no school 2015-2016) accurate and reasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Officer wrongly found three prior restorations (there was one) and no schooling in 2015-2016; transcripts show otherwise.
issues.respondent_position: Number of restorations was immaterial; one prior restoration still supported a finding of familiarity (para 21).
issues.result_quote: The Officer’s factual errors and resulting adverse conclusions are sufficient to render the Decision unreasonable.

issues.issue: Did the officer consider all relevant circumstances and evidence in exercising TRP discretion under s. 24(1)?
issues.applicant_position: Officer ignored her sworn evidence of filing attempts within the window, McMaster's late acceptance and IRCC correspondence.
issues.respondent_position: Officer had no duty to weigh all circumstances; late filing was the basis; no evidence of attempts within window.
issues.result_quote: I find that the Officer did not do so in Ms. Kazembe’s case.

issues.issue: Was the officer's process procedurally fair (notice of concerns)?
issues.applicant_position: Officer should have told her about concerns on paper restoration and study-permit compliance.
issues.result_quote: I will not assess her arguments concerning the fairness of the Officer’s process.
